KnobMacro
K1STRUCTUREon a string, its dispersion (below a quarter, a buzzing bridge; above, the partials stretched, then noise in the period); on sympathetic strings, the intervals they are tuned to; on a body, how its partials are spaced, from squeezed through harmonic to bell-like
K2BRIGHTNESSthe exciter's low-pass and the string's or body's high-frequency loss
K3DAMPINGhow long it rings, from about 70 ms to about 18 s to −60 dB, and near the top on without decay
K4POSITIONwhere it is plucked or struck and where it is picked up: which partials sound
K5EXCITATIONthe bow's or the dust's level; a strike's or a pluck's, half to twice
K6BOWthe bow's attack, up to 0.75 s shorter or longer
K7DUSTthe dust's rate, up to 30 impacts a second more or fewer
K8MUTEhow much the sound is damped when the key is released

BAYAREA — a West Coast voice

BAYAREA is a fixed-point port of the bayarea opcode of Vascular, contributed by its author. It plays from the shared pool of voices. Each voice has:

  • an oscillator that morphs from sine through triangle and square to saw (SHAPE), its frequency modulated linearly, through zero, by two sines at ratios of it (0.66 and 3.3 by default, other ratios on some sounds), each ratio wandering slightly and slowly;
  • a wavefolder (FOLDS), reflecting the wave back into range;
  • a 12 kHz smoothing low-pass and a trace of noise;
  • either a low-pass gate, where a resonant low-pass and an amplifier are struck together by one-shot envelopes (an attack of 2–3 ms and a decay), or a sustaining envelope over two resonant low-passes (an attack while the key is held, a release when it is let go). The filters sweep from 300 Hz to the sound's peak frequency, higher for louder notes;
  • a saturating output stage (tanh, then a soft clip) with its own drive;
  • a bank of three resonators (508, 270 and 1153 Hz, ringing for 1–1.4 s), mixed in by the sound's amount;
  • an LFO (triangle, ramp, square or random steps) that moves the shape, the folds, the two FM depths, the attack, the peak, the decay and the resonator mix, by amounts drawn with the sound.

Changed from the opcode: the square and saw are band-limited with polyBLEP instead of being summed from 44 partials (too costly for this chip), and the opcode's reverb is replaced by the track's sends to the master delay and reverb, keeping only its resonator bank.

KindEnvelope
BONGOgatelow peak, short decay, little folding
PLUCKgatebrighter, square to saw, short to medium decay
CHIMEgatethe upper modulator deep, long decay, resonators
FOLDEDgateheavy folding
SWELLsustainslow attack (0.3–3 s), long release
DRONEsustainslower attack (0.5–4 s), the lower modulator deep, long release

On AMBIENT, BAYAREA favours BONGO, CHIME, SWELL and DRONE. On EXPERIMENTAL it favours PLUCK and FOLDED, with more drive and folding and other FM ratios more often. The percussive kinds (CHIME, FOLDED, BONGO) end quickly and free their voices.

Macros.

KnobMacro
K1SHAPEthe oscillator from sine through triangle and square to saw
K2FOLDSthe wavefolder's drive
K3FMboth modulators' depth
K4DECAYthe gate's decay, or the sustain's release, from an eighth to eight times the sound's own
K5ATTACK1/8 to 8 times as long
K6FM RATIOboth modulators' ratios, 1/4 to 4 times
K7SPRINGthe resonator bank's mix
K8DRIVEthe output stage's drive, 1/4 to 4 times

HIVE — a swarm of oscillators

HIVE is a port of the SWARMER machine of DigiRust, contributed by its author, extended here with inharmonic and textural kinds. It plays from the shared pool of voices. Each voice has seven oscillators, and each sound draws, for every one of them:

  • its place relative to the note: the note itself, an octave or a fifth, a step of a cluster (quarter-tones, seconds), or an inharmonic partial (the modes of a free bar, a bell's partials, a stretched harmonic series, or ratios at random);
  • its share of the spread that DETUNE sets (symmetric, clustered, to one side, at random, or in pairs);
  • its wave, a position along sine, triangle, saw and square (neighbouring waves crossfaded);
  • its level, and which of three LFOs moves its pitch and its level, and at what phase. The LFOs' rates are drawn too, from about 0.02 Hz to a few Hz depending on the kind; MOVEMENT scales their depth.

The seventh oscillator is the main one, set against the other six by MIX. Each voice also has a slow noise on every oscillator's pitch; how closely it follows the key (fully for the melodic kinds, partly or hardly at all for the textural ones); noise; a ring modulation of the first oscillator by the main one; a 4-pole filter (two state-variable filters, low-pass, band-pass or high-pass) whose cutoff follows half the key's movement and is swept by its own envelope and by the first LFO; an ADSR envelope on the level; and a drive (tanh).

Changed from DigiRust: the waves are computed as they play (the sine from its table, the triangle directly, the saw and square band-limited with polyBLEP) instead of read from band-limited tables, which would not fit in RAM here; the filter, envelopes and drive are Tonitor's own. Silent oscillators are skipped; with three HIVE voices or more sounding, oscillators 12 dB under the loudest are skipped too, to save the chip's time.

Kind
SUBthe main oscillator one or two octaves down, short attack; sometimes an octave up in the swarm
LEADbrighter, short attack, resonant
STABshort attack and decay, little or no sustain, a strong filter sweep; sometimes a fifth and an octave in the swarm
PADslow attack (0.2–3 s), wide detune, long release; sometimes octaves in the swarm
DRONEslower attack, full sustain, long release (1.5–6 s); sometimes fifths and octaves stacked
WASHthe slowest attack (0.8–5 s), the longest release (3–9 s), often noise and a moving filter
CLUSTERthe oscillators at quarter-tone and semitone steps around the note, slowly beating
METALinharmonic partials (bar, bell, stretched or random), struck: short attack, a long decay, often a ring modulation
SPECTRAinharmonic partials whose levels and pitches turn slowly (or shimmer), the key hardly followed: a spectrum evolving over seconds
GROUNDtwo octaves down, a dense inharmonic cluster with noise, a slowly moving filter, driven: rumble
AIRfiltered noise and one to seven high, drifting whistles, band-pass or high-pass, the filter swept: wind
TIDESthe oscillators gliding apart and back by up to five semitones on slow LFOs, sometimes on inharmonic partials

CLUSTER, METAL, SPECTRA, GROUND, AIR and TIDES are meant for non-melodic, textural use. On AMBIENT, HIVE favours PAD, DRONE, WASH, SPECTRA and TIDES, and makes the LFOs slower, the sound darker and the attacks longer. On EXPERIMENTAL it favours STAB, CLUSTER, METAL, GROUND and AIR, and adds more noise to the pitches, more drive and, sometimes, a ring modulation. AIR is the lightest kind; LEAD the heaviest.

Macros.

KnobMacro
K1DETUNEthe swarm's spread around its places, from none to twice the sound's own
K2MOVEMENTthe LFOs' depth on the pitches, the levels and the filter, from none to twice
K3MIXthe swarm against the main oscillator; NOISE (the noise's level) on GROUND and AIR
K4CUTOFFthe filter's cutoff
K5RESONANCEthe filter's resonance
K6FILTER ENVhow far the filter's envelope sweeps it
K7RINGthe ring modulation's amount
K8SHIMMERhow deeply the LFOs move the oscillators' levels

OBRADOR — an analog polysynth

An analog polysynth voice after the Oberheim SEM and the two-voice Oberheims, written for Tonitor with OberVave (an Oberheim-style firmware for the FM-1, by zvenson) as its frame of reference; the same engine as Tonitor's on the FM-1, with four more macros here. It plays from the shared pool of voices. Per voice: two oscillators (saw, pulse or both, band-limited), the second detuned or an interval away, hard-synced or cross-modulating now and then; in the lush kinds a second voice card, detuned against the first; a drive into the SEM's 12 dB filter, its output morphing from low-pass through notch to high-pass, its resonance soft-limited; a second low-pass stage for 24 dB, or the band-pass; filter and amplifier envelopes on analog curves; an LFO that comes in after a delay; and each card's own small offsets of tune and cutoff with a slow drift. The pitch wheel bends it.

Kind
STRINGStwo cards of saws, a slow attack, a delayed vibrato: the string pad
BRASSthe envelope opening the 24 dB low-pass
PWM PADtwo pulses, their widths moving slowly
BASSthe second oscillator an octave down, the 24 dB low-pass, a plucked envelope
SYNCthe second oscillator synced, its pitch swept by the envelope
NOTCHthe filter near its notch, the LFO moving it: a phasing sweep
METALcross-modulation at an odd interval through the band-pass: bells, clangs
DRONEtwo cards a fifth or an octave apart, the cutoff and the morph moving slowly
KEYSa struck filter, no sustain
SWELLthe filter opening slowly under a held chord

On AMBIENT it is softer, slower and darker, and favours STRINGS, PWM PAD, DRONE and SWELL. On EXPERIMENTAL it is harder (more drive, more resonance, cross-modulation now and then), and favours SYNC, NOTCH and METAL.

Macros.

KnobMacro
K1CUTOFFthe filter's cutoff, four octaves either way
K2MORPHthe filter: low-pass, notch, high-pass
K3RESONANCEthe filter's resonance
K4DETUNEthe oscillators' and the cards' detune, from none to three times as wide
K5FILTER ENVhow far the filter's envelope sweeps it, 24 semitones either way
K6LFOthe LFO's depth, from none to three times; turned up, a vibrato of its own too
K7DRIVEthe drive into the filter
K8VINTAGEthe cards' offsets of tune and cutoff and their drift, from none to twice
